"The Long Dark" by Hinterland Studios is a game that challanges the player by presenting them with freezing tempertures, hard to find food sources, and constanly fighting weariness and thirst. The game is a survival game at its core where you survive in the northern Canadian wilderness fighting wolves, bears, and hunt and trap deer and rabbits. The game has a tempurture system where your character judges how hot or cold the tempurture him or her is feeling. This is based on the quality of his or her clothing, whether they are outside or indoors, whether they are experincing high amounts of wind, if they're walking outside in the night or day, and whether they are sleeping in a bed or bag or if your character is beside a fire. The location you start in is usually rich in man-made shelters, (depending on the reigon) where you can find processed foods like beef jerky, gronola bars, soda, and much more. All of these food items have a prescribed weight and calorie count, with some items (like soda) reliving you of thirst and hunger. Food and other items nessicary for survival can be found in hard to reach areas, and you may find that you have to break down other physical items to get to them. Your weariness is based on how much you have slept, while you are awake, you are constanly losing "sleep" if sleep is a resource. This meter goes up or down depending on your actions. For example, if you drink coffee, then your "sleep" meter will go up. (aswell as your thirst) Whereas if you sprint it will go down much faster. It may be tempting to sprint to the location that you heard your friends talk about, but if you're not fighting your cold meter or running from a wolf, it is much more economical to walk there instead. You can see how much daylight is left by pressing "tab" by defualt, which also displays your current tempurture, your "sleep", your thirst, your hunger, your calorire count, and your current condition. Use this information to budget how much you can explore without overextending your character.
Hunting can be very beneficial, as the animal you killed will provide hides and meat that you can use to make clothing and keep yourself alive. This review will not provide any spoilers as to how to approach bears or wolves, aswell as deers and rabbits, as it is much more fun to learn the hard way. There are many ways to find weapons and other means to hunt the animals in "The Long Dark". There is the very powerful rifle, the bow, the snare, and some other, more unconventional methods.
The game presents in User Interface (UI) in a circle (that can be accessed if the player presses space), that shows the backpack, at the center, clothing, campcraft, light sources, weapons, health, and some more. The UI is only accessible if the player presses space, as to not block the art of the game.
There are other, alternitave gamemodes other than the Sandbox, which should be accessed first, like the challanges and the yet to come and fabled story mode. It should be noted that the acheviements listed in the game list are not all there are, these are ones in the game and should you complete them, they will give a new character a passive attribute.
There are several more features of "The Long Dark", which I have either forgotten about, haven't discovered yet, or don't want to spoil. This next section will be provide my personal opinion of what should be added or removed. The things I propose to the Hinterland team for consideration is regarding the game itself. In my opinion, the game could be more realistic. Now I am not sure if this would be too much trouble or too expensive but what I think would be a great resouce of information would be to interview someone living in Alaska or Canada, as they are more or less living this life everyday.  Alternitivley, should you so choose, interview someone like a survivalist or take a survival class. Another idea would be to add a carpentry book so the player could start building structures of his or her own. Some other people have suggested and wondered why the female character doesn't have a menstural cycle, which would add a good bit of realism. Now, if the team thinks this would make the female chracter unplayable (or too gross) you could just aswell add some negitive attributes to the male chracter aswell. For example, men tend to sweat more than women, and in the frigid temputures of northern Canada, this could be deadly. On the other hand, you could simply add an option to disable the negitive/postive attributes in the settings menu. Some have said the time cycle needs to be fixed as it is strange to be thirsty after only a few minutes, but I disagree. I backpack with my Boy Scout troop alot and you need alot of calories and water. (It is recomended, however, that when you hike, your backpack is only a quarter of your weight. I'm about 130 pounds as I am only 15, so I want a backpack that is about 28 pounds.) Another realism thing that you could add would be a size system, but this could prove to be too tedious for the player. You could also add an ailment, Blisters, a serious problem if you have one. Blisters are caused by having a hiking boot that doesn't fit well and causees alot of friction in one area. The way to cure this is to use moleskin around the blister, if i remember correctly.
More systems like unrination and defecaiton could be added, aswell as answers or solutions to some questions like "How does my chracter know to wait 5 days for this deer hide to cure" or "How does this guy have calorie counts on everything" ectera. I feel solutions lie in adding more books, or maybe a new reigon that has a library.
I hoped you liked my review and I hope the Hinterland team will consider some of my suggestions. Thank you for taking the time to listen to me.

Lets set the scene here - what if you had a dream you pursued your whole life was taken from you? Your whole world revolved around it: your friendships, your identity, your routine.
That's the situation our protagonist, Hinako Shirai, finds herself in at the start of this game. Losing the full use of her right leg to a dance injury, she fears she has lost ballet forever. Friendless, and with her dream taken away from her, she must take the bold step out into the real world to try and find herself.
Alone, it doesn't seem possible - but as magical girl stories are wont to do, Hinako gets help. Help in the form of two very cute identical twins [Lime and Yuzu Shijou], each of whom grant her magical powers to become a Reflector - someone who can empathize with others emotions, help stablize them, and in the process gain super powers to fight off Demons and Gods.
Through the power of _______ [cmon, you know what goes there] these three girls set off to not only save teenage emotion, but the world itself!
Intrigued? Well color me like a crayola, lets get into it!
Much was made some of Koei's decisions with the PC graphics. Eventually though, they came right on around with some gentle, friendly, vaseline laden coaxing. This game supports up to 2560x1440p, and fits nicely (if only a tad stretched) on a 21:9 dispreigh. It almost looks native. The girls in this game shimmer and shine, and for a game that was also played on vita, this thing decently uses PC graphics to get by. It succeeds in looking straight out of a manga, and Mel Kishada did such a great job on the art.
The Common [where you do fighting as a magic girl] is beautiful, if not a bit repetitive, and the school is decently laid out. The menus and the battle layout are purdy as all heck, and they really pop and sizzle. Your "smartphone" and its "apps" are pretty and laid out in a believable way. If you ever wanted to feel like a japanese school girl (cmon, you know you did) this game nails that aesthetic nicely.
Overall it succeeds in being anime to the max, and it makes compelling SoL. Of course there are some silly hitches and movements in NPCs steps and such, but that is just the awkwardness of trying to covert something magically 2D into a 3D "real life game".
Beautiful, but not without flaw.
Magical girls battle their emotions, their day to day problems, and also fight against Demons and Dark Deities. The way you connect with your classmates and your partners Lime and Yuzu both has humor and depth, and it takes very common problems that young women have to deal with and turns them into real fights.
Things like finding your identity, being overworked, alone, stressed, and just generally wayward. These emotions physically manifest as monsters which you have to fight against, which makes it interesting to see as you build 'Bonds' and complete quests.
Ever feel like your emotions were misunderstood or mischarcterized? Well what if a whole plane of existence spawned when you felt extreme sadness? This is where the Reflectors fight, for you sake and their own.
The story mixes SoL with questions about who we are as young people, and tosses in a slight amount of fanservice for levity and humour. Just deep enough.
"Coming of Age" Darn Gust, you did it again!
I looove music. And this game makes me want to ruin my hearing permanently so that my grand kids can't nag me for cookies when I'm elderly and feeble. Seriously! It's that good.
The music really takes an interesting mix of sung japanese vocals, with nice VG  instrumental mixes, and also throws in - get this - DUBSTEP. Does it sound crazy? You bet your tuckus that it is, but it sounds amazing. Each and every track fits the situation in this game, and not only that, you can change them whenever you want in the jukebox function in the game menu.
This game is worth getting for the sound track by itself honestly, its phenomenal, and not the usual JRPG fare. It strikes out on its own and goes perfectly with the animations of this game.
After I finished the game I hung around the jukebox just listening to some of the themes. I listen to them on the commute to work.
It's really beautiful, and I recommend playing with headphones for maximum weebing out.
"There's an icebox where my Atelier used to be~" I sung, as I clicked "New Game" and commenced the BR journey. As I said in my tagline, this is a grind for friendship. You will be doing bonding and dating scenes with your friends, going out and doing girl stuff on a more VN like level - which is fun and often hilarious. Another aspect of the gameplay is walking throughout the school and solving problems - and yes, for all you lazy, tired of open worldies out there, you can fast travel from place to place. In a school. That you can easily walk places. Yassss, your spoiled.
You take on fetch quests in the school, which help you discover items and gain bond points. That in itself is pretty fun and a bit grindey, but the combat is where this game really shows its artistic chops.
You really -feel- like a magical girl fighting. It's just that type of game! The combat is fluid and seemless, and the turn-based animations really fit right into a Mahou Shojo vibe. The menus, as I said are beautiful, the characters responsive, and the combat varies from walk in the park to mildly challenging.
This is a game way more about aesthetic and story than difficulty, but the battles can give you a fair bite later on in the game. In my opinion its best if you just start off in hard mode, because you'll waltz through things otherwise.
The bonding episodes and SoL elements are hilarious, and play in well, but the combat is the most rewarding. It is complemented by the gorgeous OST and and funky enemy designs.
If you ever wanted to see your sorrow manifest as a deer....thing, well prepare to laugh and enjoy yourself!
Enemy designs are a bit repetitive, but you don't really mind, as they fit the areas you are going into, and there is just enough SoL things to balance out them feeling too samey. You'll live, and likely continue to enjoy combat until the end of the game.
In Boss Battles, things get really toasty. You can fight the help of friends, which give you special abilities and powers. One character literally kicks a can at the bosses. A can. With her foot. Into a demon/god/thing. Yep. We are -there-.
Speaking of your friend harem, these dates aren't just for fun and laughs! They reward you with fragments, which are bits of emotion that power up your emotion to - well, basically they add traits and make you stronger. They have funny names like "Rapper Heart" and also very dope ones like "The Colour of the Void".
In the more slice of life elements, you can play a small pet game called Dark Cave. There is a very, very strange achievement tied to this game, so you really want to look up some information on that, because its a bizarre and random pet game. How Bizarre and Random? Well, if you play with your pet, he might become furious at you and turn into a mustached mushroom.
There is also a crafting system, but it isn't too much of one. It's very simple, and involces you refining the fragments i brought up earlier using drops from enemies and the general area.
You level up and apply points based on how much you go on dates and how much you complete friend related missions - so the awesome combat is just for items and cinematics! I don't recommend just skipping over it though - it butters the biscuit.
A beautifully crafted and wacky game, Blue Reflection is a must have for Japanese Schoolgirl loving - SoL playing - Classic JRPG and music lovers. It's a complete package that you will either loath or love. Form a bond with it, and you might just be friends with it all the way to plat...

Oh where to start ! ive played this game since just after it was first released back in 2014 and fell in love with it almost instantly. From the first time i spawned into mystery lake with nothing more than the clothes on my back and a flare in hand ive witnessed how brutal the game is. From the begining up until the end of your characters life you are at constant odds with the world around you, freezing to death, dying of eventual starvation or dehydration and making other foolish decisions like leaving your shelter in blizzard conditions and getting lost and disorientated in the snow show just how brutal and punishing this game is.
If you are into the survival genre of games and are fed up of zombies then this is the game for you! Your enemy is the world around you, wildlife and mother nature will throw everything she has at you in order end your life.
The developer of the long dark, Hinterland Studios are the real stars, they listen to their players and community to a level i have never experienced with any other developer, ideas and feedback from the community on ways in which the game could work better are taken seriously and very often implemented into the game itself. This includes wish lists for future game mechanics or items. Occasionaly there are bugs, many of these are minor and the last time i experienced a gamebreaking bug was back in 2015. The game is also updated constantly with new exciting gameplay features and fixes which eliminate bugs, all of this builds upon an already well fleshed out game considering the game is still in alpha and i can say it is one of my favourite games of all time.
As a summary, if you are looking for a game upon which you can spend hundreds of hours playing, exploring and surviving a huge beautiful brutal open world you should buy the long dark because it has that in spades !!

One thing you should note before buying Cuphead, is that the game is not for people who play games casually, and it certainly isn't for the faint of heart. This game is the most difficult game I have ever played, to the point where I spent around an hour stuck inside of the first level, which is pretty insane. The boss battles are equally, if not more challenging than the platforming sections, and are the most fun bosses that I have ever seen in a game. Cuphead's music is brilliantly executed, mainly consisting of Jazz and Ragtime, and the sound quality is also top notch. The visuals are breathtaking, with hand-drawn animation, as well as colorful and creative characters. My only downsides with this game is the "Parry" move, which can be extremely annoying in boss fights, and also the fact that it almost feels like you need an Xbox controller in order for the controls in the game to actually feel solid. Other than that, I have no issues with the game. So if you want an amazing, colorful and rage-filled experience, go ahead and buy it.

I love this game. It's one of the first games in years that I'd been anticipating, and it was def worth it. That said, my favorite joy I've gotten from this game is seeing all the salty reviews on the MS store giving it 1/2 stars bc of how difficult it is. One person even talks about how they wish they were more informed about it before preordering. The salt is so real and I love every bit of it. Now for the actual review.
This game is a mainly boss rushesque (each level is a boss, not an actual boss rush per say) platformer with 6 sidescrolling levels. Don't let the games appearance fool you, it's hard as♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ The main thing to do is, if you think of a new strategy, why not give it a go. I spent probably 20-25~ hours on the normal mode, the rest is on achievement hunting.
The art style and music is great, I believe everything was hand drawn hence why it took hella long for it to come out and the quality shows. It's really weird seeing this style in a 2017 game. It feels like this game is a lot older. The music is great if you love old timey swing/jazz/ragtime type stuff.
The bosses take a while to get used to but I always felt good when you hear that "KNOCKOUT" from the annoucer because you earned that it. It'll take an average game probably about 700~ deaths for a completion, I'd say, depending on skill level. I think I'm pretty good at platformers I'd say, but I got my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ rocked by all of these bosses at least 10 times. That said, there aren't any fights that seem to really drag on with the exception of one towards the end but that's fine bc there's a lot of variety, if you catch my drift.
I'd say that one complaint that I'd have is that you can't progress on simple mode, which just cuts off the final stage of the boss. That said, just get good and kill the boss on normal. If all else fails, just take the health buffs and dmg reduction if needed. That and the controls kinda suck. I just switched shoot to RT so my thumb is free on A B & Y for jumping, special and dodging.
Get this game. It's dope if you like this genre.
This may be a bit of a spoiler if you want to go in completely blind, but these are just some tips for what people seem to think are some of the harder bosses and in general:
You should use the purple gun on the Bee and the Dragon, and similarily the alternate bombing gun in the birdhouse level. They make those levels a lot easier since the bosses are under you in the case of the bee and Bird, and in the case of the dragon you want to stay in the top part of the screen. That's all I'll say for actual strategy bc it's one I don't see a lot of people doing and it helps out immensely. Also, for the flying levels, the Coffee upgrade is probably the most useful as the other ones (other than health) won't really change anything while you're in the plane. The extra hearts aren't really worth the trade for damage, so I usually use th P. Sugar in normal levels. Which makes jumping a lot less dangerous in a lot of situations as there are plenty of times where you'll be under a parry object, but won't be able to double tap A fast enough.

This game is one of the best Psycological Horror games you can find. It makes a pretty good shooter too.
Now, let me explain. Have you ever had a game where it terrified you to play more? Where just looking at the title screen shook you? This will be that game. While I'm not exactly the most secure when it comes to horror games (I'm a rather easy-to-scare person) this left me thinking for quite a while. I won't spoil the plot, but for those who know,
, and it does this plot really well. It's not Doki Doki Literature Club, but it leaves a thought. If you do not care about story at all in games, the gameplay is still fantastic. The "Time Only Moves When You Move" mechanic is done incredibly well, and you feel pretty cool playing the game. Especially at the replays. (Tip before you play: If you want to see your replay, press F5 at the end of a level. It may look like it's editing a replay, but it'll show you to the sheer replay without the SUPER. HOT. flashing over the screen). However, if you're not the aforementioned one, the story will take you out of the game abruptly, and probably just when you're really getting into it.
Want some real statistics? Well, here ya go.
-Story is great
-Gameplay is fantastic
-Mechanics are handled correctly
-The premise has a theory
-The "OH SHOOT" effect. (Basically, you do something SO awesome, you gawk at it.)
-The game really doesn't have a good soundtrack to listen to, unless you call the words "SUPER." and "HOT." being yelled at you music.
-There's this one mechanic that's thrown in out of nowhere that isn't as well-baked.
-Story abruptly takes you away from the gameplay.
If you're going to buy this, don't expect a sheer shmup. There is much more than gameplay, and if you're not prepared for the story, this game will be incredibly annoying because you just want to get back to the fighting.
I give this game a 7/10.

This review is for the final released version.
You start out with 2 heroes.  Eventually you recruit 4.  And then they either die, or your power crystal explodes.
For example, on the Very Easy setting and 12 floors:
Game 1.  Made it to the 6th floor, fully equipped, lots of dust, attack mods, 4 heroes, and all of them were one hit KOs
Game 2.  7th floor, 4 heroes, wore down by wave after wave of mobs.
Game 3.  4 heroes, very little dust found, lots of unpowered rooms, overwhelmed.
Game 4.  Floor 7 again, one hit KOs again.
Game 5.  Lots of waves again
Game 6.  Floor 10...I see a glimmer in site...high level, fully equipped heroes...very little dust, so only 3 rooms of around 8 powered...and the mobs ONLY attacked my crystal, room after room after room.  Crystal exploded, costing me the game.
Don't ask about the easy setting...it is a lie.
You get the trend?  Thing is, this would be a fantastic game if it were more winnable.  Good exploration, lots of different mobs, random items and characters...I enjoyed it.  Right until I died.  Even after the first couple of deaths I enjoyed it.  And then I realized...I was just banging my head against the wall.  It didn't matter what I did, what strategies I used, how I planned my paths...I might as well be flipping a coin.

Rating 7.5/10
Overview
First Person Arcade Shooter focus on highscore and time
The Good:
+ The graphics are bright and colorful. I always like it when developers are not afraid to use color in their games. The graphics are not going to blow you away but for the type of game this is, I was surprised.
+The game has a variety of different levels broken down into 4 game modes. The first game mode (campaign) is based on achieving a highscore,this is accomplished by killing enemies, collecting essences, destorying orbs, and killing plants and chaining them together. The higher the chain the bigger the points. The other three modes are time based. You either have to collect essences,destory orbs or kill plants within a certain time limit.
+The games main focus is on replayability. If you are the type of person to replay levels to constantly get better and better and get higher and higher on the leaderboards, this is the game for you.
+In addition to all of this, the game provides plenty of powerups, i.e double damage, flight, double points etc. to make things more interesting
+ Different variety of guns to suit your playstyle, although I found only a handful of them useful.
+Achievements are somewhat easy to get.
The Bad:
-The game does not save any of your controller bindings upon startup. You have to adjust it everytime you start the game. The default setting on the controller was good enough for me, however I found this to be pretty sloppy.
-the shooting does not have the same weight and feel as other First person shooters. This is more of a minor gripe as the focus on the game isn't necessarily shooting enemies and is somewhat expected from an indie developer.
- The game can feel repetitve at times, their isn't enough in the core gameplay mechanics that would keep the game very interesting for very long
-if your not interested in getting highscores, or beating times you may find this game somewhat boring.
-A.I is a bit wierd. Sometimes they do what their suppose to do and other times they just stand there.
Conclusion:
This is a love/hate type game. I found it somewhat refreshing in the FPS genre focused on something different. I think the game deserves more attention and sales but just make sure you know what your getting yourself into.  If your expecting a fast paced game killing lots of enemies like the old days then you will be disappointed. This is more of an arcade based game that requires some thinking in how your approach the level in order to gain the most points possible. Enjoy.

Created by: WPXGAMES
What is Xotic?
Xotic is a hybrid arcade-style FPS with vividly luminous graphics and addictive game play mechanics. Eliminate the Orb’s life-sucking presence as you blast enemies, and detonate chain-reactions in a race against the clock, all while discovering secrets, collecting power ups and upgrading your skills. Xotic is an indie throwback made for modern gamers in search of originality. Hone your reflexes and develop a combat strategy that will place you at the top of the global leader board. Are you up to the Xotic challenge?
Intro Cinematic to the game Xotic, and first impressions: I really enjoyed the way WXP created the intro to this game, the cinematic. While not a lot of animation, it has a lot of beautiful graphics that help tell the story, along with the narration from the robotic voice. Right off the bat, the sound of the narrator was a bit odd, it felt as if it might not be understandable, but it was very clear in every word spoken.
The voice, rising and lowering in tone, sounding ever so strange to this brand new game, became familiar as the story unfolded about the story of the “Orb” that longed to have a physical body. I question, though, the very creation of the Orb, its origins, and its intelligence. It seems rather odd that the story starts off talking about how there is an Orb that is taking over the universe, planet by planet, but with no explanation as to how the Orb came to be, and why it possesses the capability to think and want.
The default controls start your sensitivity level at 50%, and it took some adjusting to find out, for me personally, that 90% was just right so that turning didn’t feel too slow, or too fast. As one hundred percent felt uncontrollable.
Playing through the first level, the tutorial, I felt the game really explained a lot regarding the point system, and an explanation of each item. I’m referring to the scab plants, the vase, power ups, and aerial collectibles. I, however, did not feel that the game explained well enough how to climb to greater heights to shoot, and collect, other items.
Another thing that the tutorial could have explained are the Champions that you face. I found out, the hard way, that Champions are like mini bosses in the game, that are tougher to kill, and do they more damage than regular enemies.
Playing through my first bonus round, I really got to feel a lot more of the controls and how they functioned, and a bit of the moving around while jumping. Overall, it’s really becoming pretty fun, though jumping and moving mid-air is a small feat in and of itself. It’s beneficial to get a good feel of where you want to jump, and what you wish to collect, so careful planning in some of your
maneuvers is a good idea!
Continuing on through the next levels, the game picks up in difficulty, challenging the player to really use strategic shooting, dodging, and making use of their secondary weapons, if they have one. The Champions become tougher, and throwing in machine gun-like enemies makes it even more crucial to watch where you’re standing, and to take cover in order to regenerate health if needed!
I’ve finally mastered the art of climbing higher into the air using a combination of jumping + Tab, to put the small nearly invisible shields below me, to creating platforms at just the right time for hitting those extra bonus points, and even dodging enemy attack!
The action in Xotic is very fast-paced, the music calming, even in a tough situation when things are difficult. I’m truly having a lot of fun, and enjoying using experience points to unlock new skills, increase my characters attributes, and kicking some serious♥♥♥♥♥
OVERALL SCORE: 8/10
Sound: 8/10 The music and sound effects are really great in this game, but I don’t care too much for the narrator’s voice.
Controls: 9/10 Playing through the game, everything is relatively easy to control. Aiming is great once you have sensitivity set properly, but when it comes to mid-air control and direction, this is where things just don’t feel as smooth. It’s as if you’re trying to jump while in space, with no gravity or sense of control regarding your direction.
Graphics: 8/10 The graphics in this game are beautiful, and make me feel as if the environments in the game are really alive. But this also creates a sense of confusion among all the objects your shooting. It’s hard to see the small mountains that release the bugs that explode on you, the machine gun enemies sometimes blend in with the surrounding environment, and the look of the enemies and your own character isn’t the best, but there’s nothing to really ruin the experience that I’ve had with the game.
Final Thoughts:
Xotic is a really fun, fast paced, action RPG First Person Shooter, with beautiful graphics, lovely music, and an intuitive design on combat and collecting items while constantly improving score.
The game is definitely built for the competitive player who thrives to have the highest score.
For 9.99 on Steam, Xotic is worth buying and playing through the entire game!

Xotic is a score based First person shooter. The point of the game is to get the highest score possible by doing a few things, creating long chains which net you more points, finishing the level quickly, and completing the 3 goals that each level has in order to get a 5 star rating, which also nets you more points. All of these elements combined give you aspects of speed running, score attack, and even some platforming with the "Hologram's" that you can deploy mid air and land on.
*The game has a very vibrant and neon color pallet, and while the texture quality isn't fantastic, it does still look fairly nice and should run on most systems.
*It feature one weapon with multiple different modes that all fire different projectiles (All firing modes besides the default require energy to use, this regerates on its own)
*Xotic has upgrades for each different weapon firing mode as well as upgrades for the character.
*The game is single player, but a lot of fun of the game comes from trying to beat those on the leader boards, after each level it will show your place on the leader board for the level you just completed.
*Xotic has quite a few levels that are interestingly designed and do vary a bit, the game can become repetitive, but i think thats mostly a genre related problem and not Xotic's fault. But the game is very fun in burst playing sessions (At least for me).
The game works great using a mouse and keyboard (As a FPS should), I did find that using a controller seems to have weird sensitvity issues, the Y axis is much more sensitive than the X axis, and they can not be adjusted individually, but this is not a problem for most as the keyboard and mouse work just fine.
If you're into score attack games, this is one to look at. It has an interesting setting and a very nice color pallet with good score attack mechanics.

Blue Reflection is a magical girl JRPG, a type of game I've been hoping to see for a while. It plays similarly to a Persona game, where it is split into daily life segments for getting to know the characters and otherworld segments for exploring and fighting.
The story is very character-focused, which works to its favor. Most of the story involves the main character gaining power through empathizing with others, allowing herself and those she meets to grow. This power is used to fight supernatural monsters from outer space and the negative emotions they impose on an otherworld sustained by humanity's collective unconscious. While there is an overarching plot, it doesn't get much play until near the end of the game. More information than that goes into spoiler territory, so that will be addressed later.
The "daily life" gameplay is very similar to the Persona series, albeit simpler and more streamlined. Outside of story chapters, free time can be spent exploring the school, completing side quests, or spending time with friends. There are several interesting things you can find in the school, particularly an odd collectible-like system where finding glowing spots in the school will open up new topics for the main character's IM app. Side quests involve either jumping into the otherworld to fight monsters/collect items, or simply bringing items to the person in question. While simple in design, each side quest has an interesting hook to give context to the mission, and so it's interesting to see what each student has problems with. Spending time with friends works similarly to Social Links/Confidants in the Persona series, where you get special events at certain levels of affection. During some of these events, the player may get a choice on how to respond, which changes the skill the player earns from completing that event. There is also a system where, at the end of each day, the player can decide what to do at night, which can cause certain events to play the next morning (sometimes giving stat boosts). There's no real time limit to free time, so it's possible to complete everything except for alternate scenes in a single playthrough.
The other gameplay for the game takes place in "The Common", an otherworld that is shaped by the collective unconscious. Because of its nature, it is split into certain "zones" such as Joy and Fear. Here the player fights monsters and prepares to fight the "Sephirot", giant monsters from outer space. The basic exploration will be familiar to those who have played the Atelier games, since it involves the same kind of on-screen monster icons and the ability to find items in certain areas. Battles are turn-based, though there are some interesting systems unlocked later in the game that make the wait time between turns an active part of the battle (such as allowing the use of a special meter to heal or accelerate turns). Instead of having XP, the game uses "growth points" to level up, which are gained exclusively from story progress and spending time with friends in daily life. This reduces some of the grind found in other JRPGs. On the other hand, it's easy enough to grind growth points from spending time with friends that combat will be easy for most of the game, even on the hardest difficulty. Each character also learns far more skills than you will ever need to use, and some skills end up being redundant because of this. While there is a system for learning specific skills in the growth point system, whatever combination of level ups you decide on will end up leaving you more than powerful enough to win. This is made even easier since HP/MP is restored after each fight. Battles can still be fun once you've become overpowered, but don't go into the game expecting something as difficult as a Megami Tensei game.
The last major gameplay element involves fighting the giant bosses. These are 2-3 phase fights that involve a single large enemy with multiple parts. You can finish each phase just by killing the main part, but each sub-part you kill will be inactive for a while and cause a debuff to the main body. These fights also allow the non-magical friends of the main character to support the team, usually with small buffs or attacks that increase the special gauge (which allows for certain abilities between turns later in the game, as mentioned earlier). These fights are usually about as easy as the rest of the game, but may take a bit longer due to high HP and the need for the player to heal.
Overall, it's a fun magical girl RPG, though not something for anyone looking for a challenge. This is very much a game focused on the stories of its major characters, with the main story and battles as part of the experience (but not the focus).
A note on the PC port: The game no longer has a game-breaking crash thanks to a patch, but it still is pretty resource-hungry and can crash under certain conditions. If you don't have a pretty recent computer, it may be better to look into the PS4 version.
I was going to include a spoiler section where I review the story a bit, but it ran into the character limit for reviews. I may end up posting the full version of this review elsewhere, then linking to it in the comments. For now, hopefully the spoiler-free version will be enough.

This game "Xotic" (pronounced exotic), although I continually call it zotic for some unknown reason, is a splendid blend of bejeweled meets unreal tournament. The focus here is on scoring and making the most of the multiplyers within each of the many differing score attack levels there are in the game. Usually, there are 3 goals to complete to attain a perfect 5 star rating for your actions during gameplay. Those goals are: gathering all the essence, eliminating all the scabs, and finding all the brains. Essence is a colorful diamond type figure dotted around the levels and can be acquired by running through them. The scabs are red rooted circles in the ground that you must shoot consecutively to form chains which increase your point scoring potential. Finally, the brains are mysterious objects that float and explode once shot and resemble a fireworks effect that is usually fairly awe inspiring. There are also essence, brain, and scab attack modes that challenge the player to complete the level in the quickest time possible. The scoring system for all phases of the game is superb, as well as the leaderboard system. Although this is a challenging game, its a breakthru product as far as first person shooter scoring games go.

Project Zomboid is one of my favourite games that I'll return to again and again, sometimes with the same old file and sometimes with a completely new one depending on how inefficiently I'll play the game.  This game is more than just a 'kill zombies and survive' game.  It's an immersive, diverse, thought-provoking game that at times will leave you frustrated, and so intensely real feeling.  Every time you start over you're in a different place on the map.  And with recent updates, there are more maps so you'll be just as likely to get lost and swarmed by a horde.  There are times when I play this game that I'll be alone, in the dark with headphones and just hearing that noise when you see a zombie will be enough to scare the daylights out of me; this game is that kind of pull-you-in game.  And on top of all that, there are the decisions you'll have to make while playing the game.  Your house was broken into while you were asleep?  Do you jump out the window and risk a broken limb or take on the zombies with your damaged bat.  There's a medical building but it's already been swarmed by a mass of zombies.  Are the medical supplies really worth it?  And the hordes.  You can risk shooting them with an impressive gun to kill off at least half of them before they attack you, but the noise will only bring about more zombies.  All in all, this game is one I simply can't put down, with a high replayable value, that knocks all the other zombie survival games out of the park with its ingenuity.  It's one you shouldn't resist playing, and for an excellent price.

Where to begin.
I've played enough of TLD to know the ins and outs of how to survive, I've lived long enough to know that I could survive forever, I've become good with the bow, crafting, found most of the locations, and so on. I always kept this game in the back of my mind, to come back to, as it gets closer to being completed.
But at this stage, despite the devs good intentions, it feels bad. Really bad.
The problems most survival games have is balance and pacing, and becoming inevitably repetitive / nothing to do. The reason for this is largely because most games take the entire genre from the standpoint of "Naked and Afraid", give the players nothing to begin with, and have them do everything from scratch. And while this works well with certain games / settings, it's awful in TLD, even with the minimal gear they give you.
It's terrible when you cant survive day 1 because a fire simply wont light over a dozen times at 60% chance with no storm and blocked from the wind. It's worse when you cant survive day 2 because you have everything you need except matches because of day 1, so you have no way whatsoever to light a fire. 60% chance to light, my♥♥♥♥♥ And this is on VOYAGER! (normal difficulty). Good luck crawling to explore to try to find a freaking match.
Further, as you explore, if you are able to, you just find everything you could ever want lying around the indoor areas. This has always bugged me. Why even go outside once you find some nice buildings? And once you know where everything is, what then? Just go grab the best stuff, and all of a sudden the entire game is pointless. Paradoxically everything is just sitting there, so if you get to it, it's too easy, but if you can't light fires, to get there in the first couple of days, game over. So the game just becomes an excecise of restarting enough times to know where to get stuff easily by memorizing the map (which is never randomized).
That's a dumb game in a nutshell,
(completion bar for fires, sleeping, etc) for long periods of time.
unrealistic aspects of a game that's supposed to be realistically brutal, terribly handled, terrible combat, terrible everything. I am quite surprised to find that the dev has basically gone nowhere on wolves, they are still total ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥t. And yes, putting in a blurb in the intro that "We know wolves do not normally attack people in real life" doesn't make it any better.
Meanwhile, in a game like The Forest, I'm getting 60fps lock, with photorealistic graphics and amazing effects. Isn't the point of the minimal, cardboard-like graphics in TLD partly so that you dont have these fps performance issues?  Seems like they just can't code it to where it's acceptable. And if the counter-argument is "it's not optimized because early access lol" I for one do not give half a♥♥♥♥♥♥about that. It is what it is. If it sucks, it sucks.
Crawling at a snails pace, knowing the game is pointless because you'll never find matches before you die, is a crappy time. Just grabbing the best gear because you know where it is already is a crappy time.
Oh, and thanks for
by the way. Shouldn't have that been thought of by now? Talk about fatigue... to my damn wrist, that is. Do these devs ever play their own game? Surely you must know that jamming W while moving at 30% speed for minutes at a time, getting nowhere, is♥♥♥♥♥
"But it's realistic" well
And I've turned the corner on this and concluded that the realism does not make up for the pain of playing this 'game'. It's weird, I talked with 2 friends recently who have been big fans of this game in the past, as was I, (i've had it for about 2 years), and one was talking about the seemingly steady progress, and the other was like 'screw that game'. I am very surprised that I agree with the latter. Maybe times have changed, maybe TLD hasn't changed enough, maybe I've changed. But this just isn't fun, and time's up for me to give this rating a longer leash.
When TLD first came out it was one of the few real-feeling survival games out there. Now, years later, there are dozens of contenders, and many which are more worth your time than this. Right now I'd recommend The Forest; just turn the world generation settings to "Peaceful" if you don't want the horror / cannibal part of it, and enjoy a pretty well done survival experience, they even have cold / snow biomes, arguably more extensive crafting, and it goes on sale for 10 bucks.

You won't find this in any review but I very much thought this game was the peak of the series. It took them 4 games to create the engaging, visceral, destructive experience they were going for here and with the culmination of all of the lessons they have learnt, Violition has managed to create the most empowering third person shooter ever. Stasis in this game makes Isaac Clarke look like a noob, it not just stops enemies but drains their health and replenishes yours. The Mechs from F.E.A.R. were awesome? Nope, they cant quite charge through a wall, crush all the enemies in the way and cause the building they just went through to collapse. What's a gravity gun again? The Magnet gun is my favourite gun ever (along side the Portal Gun). This is the power-fantasy any crazy like me has been waiting for. Sniper shooting at you? Shoot a magnet at the base and another at the roof. The base flies upwards into the roof and the whole thing implodes and then collapses. Survive that! Boss fights consist of throwing the boss around the enviroment or pieces of the environment at them until they are impaled by debris and their body parts scatter with a gratifying splat. The campaign does get tedious towards the end though, with one long mission underground with no destructible environments and the story takes itself more seriously than I can. But Horde mode and a free form destroy everything 'Ruin Mode' provides some online fun. Valve better start working on Half Life 3 or everyone is just gonna rip off the old games and forget about them. R.I.P. Gravity Gun.

You know what? Evolve isn't for everyone. You need half a brain and two or more buddies to play with. If you don't have anyone to play with or like playing solo? Take a few hours to learn how to play the monster. When I first started, it took me and my buddies a good five to ten hours of playing to find the classes and roles we like to play.
People are complaining about the money for the game and DLC. If you don't like it, DON'T BUY IT~! Go back to playing free to play games. Do you really think these people build us games for the goodness of their hearts? Get real. They are looking to make money like everyone else and put food on the table.
People complain about replay value? Has anyone complained about CS replay value or BF replay value? Hell even COD replay value? My god, looking into league of legend~!!! They have the same three maps for the last SIX YEARS~! Yet people still play it.
IF you are someone that does complain about replay value? I don't think FPS are for you mate. You should head back to RPG's
Evolve is the same as all those games but instend of 5v5 or 16vs16 or 32vs32 matches. It is 4v1. Myself I don't buy FPS for single player mode. I play FPS to play with my friends. If there is single player mode? I use it to get my video/mouse settings in order. This isn't 1993 where you played Doom in your parents basement~! You are not on dail-up~!! (and if you are? I cry for you) FPS now a days are mostly about online PvP. IMO I think Evolve is a nice change to the Run and Gun / Spray and Pray FPS. Evolve gets you thinking.
I hear people calling Evolve a running sim? Well how else to you get from point A to point B? I love the Jet Packs and scaling the map. It reminds me of Tribes. There is no reason why if you have a GOOD trapper, you shouldn't be on the monster 24/7. I know it is hard to do but if you play Evolve, YOU NEED TO THINK~! It is NOT a Run and Gun / Spray and Pray game like CS/BF/COD to name a few. You just can't go running blindly into the wild.
Speaking of Wild. Damn nature you scary~!! That was one of the selling points to this game for me. The environment CAN KILL YOU~! If you are a player that likes to run off by yourself? GG. But don't get me wrong. There are times when you need to break off to cut off the monster as a trapper or cut across the map to catch up with the team. However, you need to be careful of what is around you. One miss step is the difference between trapping a monster and trapping yourself in a plant or a death roll. Plus the weather can change the map. Rain can be a monsters best friend.
Over all the game is great to play with friends or even solo. Just because there are only a few maps/hunters/monsters now, doesn't mean that is it. Once you find a class and role to play. Learn them all for that class. If played RIGHT~! you don't need to worry about progression at all. The progression is there way of teaching you how to play that hunter. Every hunter has its role to play and some hunters work better with other hunters. Test it out. Don't just play Five hours of the game and say it is garbage.

I usually don't buy into the hype of video games before release, but I thought I'd give this one a shot and shelled out $80 for the extra hunters and monster that will unlock in a future patch.
Unfortunately, I regret that decision.
There are a few technical issues and a host of design flaws I see in this game that make it not a serious contender for long-term play in my opinion. This is aside the fact that a AAA-title game selling for $60 came only with a very linear multiplayer game mode. There is no single-player campaign or any other mode except a singlular multiplayer experience repackaged as multiple game modes (as if playing bots in 5 maps consecutively makes a "campaign" mode). I felt a bit robbed by that. It'd be one thing if there was a lot more depth in the game with regard to the classes or gameplay, but this game's multiplayer just feels unsophisticated.
Don't get me wrong, I have nothing but respect for Turtle Rock Studios and think they made something cool here, but I think they need rethink some of their designs if they want this game to have any staying power.
The game is surely fun for the first many hours (I definitely put my fair share in) but the current design issues eventually push away all but the most dedicated fans. Don't take it just from me, look at the numbers yourself:
Wait for it to get down to ~$15 with all DLC, then it'll be an OK buy.

Cuphead is a beautifully intense run-and-gun platformer that pays homage to the Golden Age of Animation (e.g. 1930s Disney and Fleischer) and puts your reflexes to the test in a wacky cross between Mega Man and Gunstar Heroes.
In this perilous cartoon adventure, you play as Cuphead and/or Mugman on a mission to collect wayward souls after losing a bet with the Devil himself. Thus, you will be pitted against over 20 crazy bosses, each with their own unique design and attack patterns.
Throughout this journey, you'll be armed with one or two weapons at a time (which can be shot in 8-directions), a Megaman-X-style dash, a mid-jump parry (for absorbing and/or operating pink objects) and a Super button for pulling off special moves.
Each separate boss battle usually lasts 2-5 minutes, but every second counts. In each battle, you must take down the boss without losing all your health points (i.e. 3 minimum, 5 maximum), or else you'll have to start the fight from the beginning. Thankfully, you have infinite lives, so there's no need to worry about dying too many times.
Regardless, it can be both frustrating and maddening to lose repeatedly to the same boss, especially when you get so close to beating it. If that weren't enough, each time you lose, the game even shows you how close you are to beating it, accompanied with the boss mocking you. But, on the brighter side, it makes the joy of finally overcoming said boss all the more satisfying. Never before have I experienced this feeling so many times in one game.
This game also features 6 tricky platforming stages in which you can collect coins to spend on unlockable weapons (e.g. spread fire, charge shot, etc.) and charms (e.g. 1-2 extra health points, invincible dash, etc.). These stages are a nice change of pace from the onslaught of boss battles. You can also find hidden coins by exploring certain places and carrying out certain tasks on the world map.
I personally had high hopes for this game ever since its teaser came out, and the final product has exceeded my expectations with its combination of fluid hand-drawn animation and toughs-as-nails action gameplay. Because of this, it was hard for me to be angry no matter how many times I failed at one boss or another.
For me, this game's greatest strength is that it entices its players to keep trying and trying again until they win. And, after you finally triumph over a boss and feel the ecstatic joy of victory, it's then a matter of testing yourself to do better.
However, this could've been a perfect game if it had more game modes than just its main story (i.e. lots of boss battles, a few platforming stages), particularly a survival mode or one or more competitive 2-player modes (e.g. race, shooting gallery, etc.). This game features 3 unique stages in which you must parry waves of pink ghosts from an urn in order to unlock a super special move. Unforunately, once you've completed each stage, you can never play them again (unless you start a new game). It would've been nice if this game had an endless mode with those stages in mind, because it would make the perfect break from the usual running and gunning.
So, all-in-all, I consider "Cuphead" a colorful rollercoaster of cartoon carnage that will make you laugh, shout, cry and cheer from start to finish (as it made me and many others). Brace yourselves, casual and hardcore gamers alike, you'll be in for a bumpy ride that you'll never forget!

The only question I have is why I can't murder other heroes to loot them. The rest of my questions have all been killed out of me.
I didn't think I'd like a roguelike this much. Maybe this and FTL have a secret hold on me. When it comes down to what you like about them, the challenge or the exploration, I think I like this game better as the challenge doesn't rely entirely on totallyrandom generation. Imagine if you could improve your ship in FTL without needingit all to come from shops or random encounters, but also gave you the options of directly influencing the parts of your ship with scrap, reinforcing the hull or weapons by themselves. That's what the heroesin this game fillthe gap on. Mixing it with tower defense makes this game engaging as you try tokeep heroes inbetween monsters and your crystal ala Dungeon Defenders, and executes it with the power sent to each grid. Managing these, your heroes and your defense network makes the game engaging.
I would like to see more ships added. I enjoythe fact you can have certain gains and deficits granted by each pod, but if the developer doesn't make some whacky options available, or powerful ones, then the gimmick is short lived. I may be the only one who wants to see strange and fantastic options anymore, though. The excitement of seeing the doors open (as this is a door opening simulator, not a monster defense game as one would assume) is sadly reduced once you've run the gambit of monsters. I would like to see more happen.

Graphics: 8/10 Very pretty in game environments, monsters are varied but fit thesame subcategories, heroes continue to surpirse me in some ways. But the lit rooms sometimes offer little more than the dark ones did other than lack of gnawing death.
Sound 9/10: As with games of this nature, sound effects are re-used oftenbut it doesn't grate the ears. Music is appropriate, well done, and generally pleasing.
Overall: 9/10: Would open more doors.

I had a couple of glitches, but they went away with a simple reloading of the game, so I can't really complain about anything here.  Definitely worth the dollar if it's what you're into.

This game is ridiculously hard -- probably mostly because I'm too manly to play on the recommended "Too Easy" setting.  So, so, so so hard.  As a roguelike tower-defense game, it's a resounding success.
Amplitude has put the same care and ability into this game as they have in both Endless Space and Endless Legend -- games I also recommend for their streamlined, engaging 4X glory.  I'm not here to talk about them, though.
Dungeons of the Endless is fun.  Until it wrecks your face.  At which point -- for me -- the pain of defeat is assuaged by the promise of another dungeon dive.
To be forthright, there are some issues with the game.  I commonly experience what I assume is a bug with purchasing items from merchants, and with swapping items amongst my heroes.  I don't know if there's a gameplay element I'm missing -- because as far as I can tell, there's no documentation for the game, which is frustrating -- or if it's, as I'm guessing, some faulty programming.  It's not anything bad enough to preclude me from recommending the game.
In closing, I'm looking forward to where this new hybrid genre hopefully leads.  There are hints of real brilliance not quite realized by this outing -- more focus on establishing safe-routes and requiring their use during escape; emergency one-off Dust powers for the ridiculous unbeatable hordes which have spelled my doom pretty much every playthrough; perhaps some micro-tactics control to allow for more intelligent defenses than the current auto-targeting system allows; it'll be interesting to see.
To encourage Amplitude to explore their options further:  buy the game!  You'll like it, if you know what's good for you.  Even when it's tearing your face off.

The way I see it is that this is a slice of life take similar to Persona, where the bonds of friends overcome the enemies.
Pros:

+

+

+
: I've only played the game in Hard mode and I can say that it wasn't the hardest, but I consider that a good thing. The game is similar to Atelier in terms of battles, with the additional mechanic of ether, which allows one to expend it for skills or for overdrive to get additional turns.
Neutral:
=
: The game is really focused on story, so chances are, you won't stay in the common (dungeons) that long. Added the fact that you don't get any EXP or currency for defeating enemies, makes it so that there's not much point in staying in there. Which is good in the way that there isn't any grinding done. There's no need for currency as there really are no shops in the game.
=
: They aren't stressed upon that much, but they have two distinct usages (aside from one item): to temporarily increase stats or permanently increase stats and are not usable in battle. This is one less thing to think about, but it just seems like it's missing a lot.
=
: Mentioned by a commentor, this game is not difficult. It has three modes, but even at the highest difficulty (HARD), it does not require you to think that hard. I personally liked the casual difficulty, but it could be something of note for people to think about.
Cons:
-
: They're repetitive. They're mostly either story missions, find shards in the common or defeat mobs. Painfully obvious in chapter 10.
-
: Also known as dungeons in the game, there are 4 basic types of them,
They're generally tiny and have common themes with them. The only exception is in chapter 10 with the final few missions, which places you in a very large area for some reason.
-
: It's there. However, as items are not really that stressed upon, it isn't something that will make or break the game. It's a feature that could have been much better.

Blue Reflection lets players control Hinako Shirai, a regular student by morning, a magical girl after class and a victim of questionable cutscene camera angles all the time. The gameplay and story largely take place in two distinct settings, Hoshinomiya high school and a fantasy realm called The Common.
School is the non-combat section of the game, the gameplay there consist of talking to NPCs, receiving (or reporting) quests and watching a lot of cutscenes. (yes with a lot of questionable camera placements). The Common is  dungeon crawl section where players get to fight enemies along with two other party members, Yuzu and Lime. The combat is usual turn-based JRPG, and even though enjoyable, often feel predictable and too easy even at hardest difficulty. Spamming attacks with knockback effect and putting party in constant healing will result in victory everytime. A bit boring, but being a new IP, I imagine the scaling down of difficulty is just Gust trying to make the game accessible for as many audience as possible, probably to appeal those who play non-combat games like the visual novel or dating-sim crowds (which the game clearly borrowed lots of elements from). Content-wise, Blue Reflection is nowhere near bad, but not exceptional either. And seriously the 'fanservice' needs to be toned down, it's on uncomfortable level here. Mahou shoujo genre is almost always about innocent girls being burdened with heavy task of saving the world and never about ogling underage girls taking shower. Do better, Gust (and don't submit to Koei Tecmo pressure to make every game another Dead or Alive Beach Volleyball either)
Art and presentation is where Blue Reflection excel the most and the main reason I purchased it. Faithful to mahou shoujo aesthetic, Blue Reflection is a very beautiful and colorful game. Every visual aspects in the game could make players scream '
' all day long. The use of photorealistic environment with anime characters fits the whole two worlds concept; Mel Kishida's character design translated perfectly in 3D form while still retain the illustration-like charm; and the user interface, just look at the them bby. It's probably the most amazing game UI I've seen, like a cross-bred between MS Metro UI with Google Material color palette.
It's awesome and ultimately looks far more 'crafty' than those template-like UI made with Scaleform. lol. (anyway, RIP Scaleform †). Oh, and the game soundtrack is fire. Art and presentation-wise, Blue Reflection is fantastic, I fall in love with it <3
Technical is where the game falls flat and can be summarized in single sentence:
. While there are some improvements from previous Gust/KT ports, like resolution no longer locked in 1080p and somewhat stable framerate. There are still no meaningful PC-exclusive features. Every adjustment must be done driver-level or by tweaking the config file. Some users even reported crashes, though I haven't found any, since patch 1.02.
In conclusion, Blue Reflection is a beautiful magical girl game with decent gameplay, but with ugly porting job and questionable amount of 'fanservice' (whatever that thing is). The way I see it, the game is a bit experimental title for Gust, being a new IP and all. There are clearly lots to be improved from this game, but I give it a free pass this time around, since it's rare to see mahou shoujo genre gets video game treatment, after all. I keep praying to all the magical girls in all the realms that Gust will revisit this world and characters again with better effort next time.

The combat has a lot going on. On hard, the early game is quite challenging and then it gets progressively easier as you level up. But it never gets boring. You're always balancing ether charges, weaknesses and pushbacks.
If you look at the screenshots and think "Wow this game looks gorgeous and looks right up my alley but is the gameplay good enough to hold it up?" then yes it is definitely worth a buy.

I made a playthrough of the game:

So first thing I'm going to do here is cover the negatives of the game, firstly that there are some issues regarding stairs which likely won't be fixed.  Seems more noticeable if you play the Sylph race (which happens to be my race, yay -.-)  Aside from that, the combat seems simple, the emotes are a bit lacking, if the game crashes, any ui or options you changed revert (you can use the /saveui command to prevent that and force save your keybindings and such), the Steam version seems to crash a lot and the linking page issue, and there's a good chance you'll be starring in tentacle porn when you meet Supergrass.
Now that those are out of the way, the game is very charming, the graphics are old, but stylishly so, the class system is unique while a few jobs should probably be renamed in my opinion (Wizards should be Priests, Doctors should be Vampires >.>), the community is great, sure we get a few nuts here and there, but for the most part, everyone is very helpful and if they can aid you, likely will.  There is a relationship system that adds various abilities which can be triggered if certain conditions are met, the item shop is mostly items you can live without, aesthetic items, and pets, but there are plenty of people who often sell some cash shop items through their own stalls.  It's a huge game with lots to do, it's not all about fighting monsters.  People who like business and making money can utilize the Commoner and Merchant classes as well as alchemy to create items to sell, people who like playing games can often join events that happen frequently throughout the day, if you enjoy hunting for treasure, you can get treasure maps and find chests with tons of booty (buy yourself a pirate costume and be a Blade Master to complete the pirate theme, arr!), if you prefer just hanging out, you can just chill in town and talk with people through Broadcast like a giant chatroom, if you like hunting big monsters, there's plenty of those lying around.  If you like being strategic or designing unique class sets, you can do that as well, mix and match any class with other class skills until you find that perfect combination you like.  If you enjoy cosplaying, plenty of characters can be designed through cash shop costumes, in-game armors, and even mixing classes together to complete your characters skills.
So you should certainly try this game if you want something more relaxed and with a good community.  What I mentioned are in-game things, but some guilds add to the list doing various things and also giving you a group of instant friends who share a similar interest as you.  Some prefer doing stuff like hunting big monsters and being the best (like Prestige) others are just more friendly and prefer hanging out (like Muffins).
And insert shameless plug here:  I'm working on my own guild as well called the Crimson Clerics, to pick up where Rifa'iya
left off many years ago.  It's a large-scale operation guild focused on helping the populace with 5 sections of assistance:  Military to hunt down newbie killers like Leech Lich and Supergrass, Teachers to find newbies in town and help them out, teaching them how to play the game, Item Management which will focus on getting items, finding/creating equipments to help people, Guild Management which will put efforts into helping level and expand the guild (as well as recruitment), and Events which will focus on setting up in-guild and out-of-guild events, anything from setting up a play to entertain people to running newbie help events where we sell cheap newbie equipment and help people with finding a career they can be proud of.

If you ignore the fandom (which I had no idea even existed until long after I finished with this first title) this is a fun game. The lore/story has to be inferred and guessed at, but it's actually deeper than you'd think for a game like this.
Creepy atmosphere, nerve-wracking moments... This game is worth the asking price, in my opinion.
You play as a nighttime security guard at a family themed pizza parlor with animatronics. Your task is to survive the night. You're given access to cameras all around the building, and you have two doors on either side of you that you can shut (at the cost of power, for some weird reason) and lights you can turn on and off to check the darkness.
It's a very simple set of gameplay mechanics, but there's also something deeper - you can't just close the doors and wait for daylight, obviously, or you'll run out of power very quickly, and then you're screwed. The camera system is vital to gameplay - you need to monitor certain rooms, and sound cues also help you figure out when things are... changing.
A rather cerebral game for such an incredibly simple premise. Jumpscares still manage to be freaky after all this time. Probably because of the earsplitting sounds, but hey - that's part of the fun.
In summary: Ignore the creepy fandom surrounding this game and perpetuated by lonely 12-year-olds who completely miss the point that this is supposed to be creepy and not some kind of furry lovefest.
If you can get past that, it's actually pretty great. I suggest watching the "Game Theories" video about it (part 1 and 2) but ignoring every other video on their channel.

Dungeon of the Endless is honestly a game I never thought I'd enjoy. As someone who doesn't care much for pixel art or rogue-likes, I was shocked that this game actually stole my heart. The art is beautiful, the gameplay is fast, tense, and even suspenseful at times. Its humor is top-notch. Even its characters themselves are endearing. +Pros
-Fast paced gameplay. Definitely intense!
-Clever take on Tower Defense.
-Loyal to the Endless setting. Its even referenced in other Endless titles.
-Beautiful aesthetics. Especially the shading and models. No two designs feel bland or too similar.
-Rewarding Co-op. It offers so much power to the players.
+Cons
-Researching is unnecessarily difficult in certain floor generations.
-Multiplayer servers occasionally act up and disconnect players. You can't rejoin a lobby either.
-The music, while excitingly curious, is somewhat limited. Could benefit from a few more tracks.

Clunky glitchy, god awful. I Have 550 hours on this game. maybe a hundred of those were me being too tired to shut down the game properly at 4am and just letting it idle.
No other rts has given me this experience. The defence on multiple fronts, the ever pressing need for better weapons, the heartbreak that fills me when one of my capital ships detonate, all hands lost. it is just amazing. ive played maybe a half a dozen mods, conquered the galaxy repeatedly using various factions. its all just so darn good.
if you are an rts nut, this game is a must. if you are a casual player who wants something they can come back to and play this is a must. if you enjoy the modding scene, this is a must.
Tips: don't auto resolve with ships in orbit, tech up before going on the offensive, build mines only on planets with a 50 or higher base income, and set a timer so you dont accidently play all night.
MODS: most mods can be installed by creating a mods folder in ypur corruption folder, and then click and dragging the mod you downloaded into the mods folder. took a few tries but i got it down, some mods are weird, but not usually worth the extra effort. uninstall mod by clicking and dragging the file out of the folder. i just saved mod authors like 60 comments with that i swear to god.
MODS, as witnessed by moi
Republic At War (RAW) while well polished visually, it is horribly unbalanced. republic easy campaign is 20 hours at the least. Cis Hard campaign was 8. i kid you not this mod is not finished balance wise.
Clone wars mod is like the 2008 series. crashes occasionally, but better than RAW
Clone wars sub-mod has great Land combat just like the 2003 cartoon, but space battles are meh.
Thrawns Revenge is pretty epic and very unique. exact opposite of RAW really. Very well balanced, but the visuals are not as good. granted unlike RAW this game isnt advertised as finished and gets a new beta in febuary of 2017
Rise of the mandalorians is both interesting, stable, and Pretty to look at. also has the BEST turrets on ships unlike in vanilla and many other mods (again, RAW)
Awakening of the rebellion seems like a dumpster, it has so much content from so many creators that it lacks stability. also has an annoying change to the way the camera works in space that ruins the top down atmosphere. overwrites your data folder for vanilla, thus requiring  a load of fiddling to uninstall.
Ultimate Corruption feels like an expansion. it balances ship strength and fighter complement by class (light cruiser, cruiser, heavy cruiser, battlecruiser) allowing for you to pick and choose what you like. adds loads of new ships, makes stations awesome, and utterly destroys x wings.
in closing, this game is ok vanilla, but fan made content shines it to a gleam.

A pants-♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ly immersive multiplayer experience. Nothing will ever top the feeling of:
- Creeping through a bombed-out apartment block in Stalingrad with a fellow soldier, only to hastily dive to cover as he gets sniped through the throat and spends several seconds bleeding to death, twitching and gurgling on the floor in front of you.
- The clumsy, slow process of manning a position inside a tank; adjusting the cannon for range, angling your tank's position towards incoming fire for maximum chance of deflecting rounds, supporting friendly infantry, staying alert for enemy anti-tank soldiers or pioneers laying ambushes, and much more.
- Picking off an opposing soldier at 150+ meters with a regular bolt-action rifle.
- Sneaking up to a fortified building, methodically crawling and sprinting from cover to cover until you can finally blow a hole in the wall with a satchel charge, allowing friendly assault troops to storm it.
- Cowering alone in the basement of a building as you hear gunfire, footsteps, and angry enemy voices directly above you.
- When the clip in your bolt-action rifle runs dry at the exact same second an enemy soldier appears a few meters in front of you, leaving you with no option but to scream and charge him, sticking your bayonet between his ribs.
- Rubber grenade physics that get you blown up more often than the enemy you're throwing it at.
- Stinking fascists.
- Bolshevik swine.
- So, so much more.
This is one of my all-time favorite FPS games. It's very difficult if you're playing against competent humans due to unforgivingly realistic damage (one rifle shot to center mass is all it takes, or even a pistol shot to the heart), movement (enjoy your winded soldier's arms shaking as you try to line up that 100m shot), and ballistics (better zero in those sights), but that just makes it so much more rewarding when you do kill that machine gunner or capture that strategic point to win the round. If you enjoy a dose of realistic masochism with your shooter action, I'd recommend this 100%.
As for Rising Storm, I haven't played it at all so I can't comment there.

I admit that I’m not a big fan of Tower Defense games. I don’t see the appeal but somehow Dungeon of the Endless drew me in. Maybe it’s the Rogue-Like tendencies and the dungeon crawling aesthetic, but I was instantly intrigued by what this game had to offer. You play as a slew of heroes who have crash landed inside of a strange dungeon. The goal is to explore and defend your ships' power generator as you  head to the next floor. Does Dungeon of the Endless accomplish the combination of tower defense and exploration well? Let’s find out in this Bullet Point Review!
What we liked
Pixel Perfect – The visuals in Dungeon of the Endless excels at providing a fluorescent sci-fi atmosphere to lose yourself in. The sleek pixel animations of characters and minimalist level design convey a truly splendid artistic wonder.
The Sound of a Journey – Without a doubt the wispy tones of the soundtrack carry the heroes on their way to adventure. It’s a euphoric tickle of the ears that saturates us in unique and calming melodies. It reminds me of a few Chrono Trigger songs, and that my friends is high praise!
Engrossing Exploration – The combination of RPG elements, Rogue-Like mazes, and Tower Defense feels just right in Dungeon of the Endless. Each door leads to a room that is randomly generated on each play session. The use of a power grid structure to illuminate the area and fortify a room is fanciful fun. Hunkering down to begin hoarding resources and plotting your escape is highly addicting. I always wanted to see what the next room had in store, even if it only lead to more monsters.
No don’t open that door – Opening doors count as turns that activate enemy waves, complete research, and restore skill based moves for the heroes. It's an interesting take on turn-based strategy.
Smart Automation – Combat is an automatic affair but it isn’t the type to frustrate you with dumb A.I. routines. The heroes will not allow enemies to stand on the other side of the room and destroy the precious generator. They make sure to keep all essential hostiles dealt with, so that you don’t have to break out into a rage festival.
Tons of characters – The heroes aren’t necessarily deep characters in terms of backstory, but each of them have specific skill sets, designs, and animations to represent their personalities. It feels good to find a new survivor in the dungeon and bring them into the fold.
Bring some friends – The Multiplayer allows up to four people to go online and survive some dungeons together. It copies the single-player fairly well, and gives each player their own resources for surviving the harsh monster attacks.
What we didn’t like
Weapon bug – Players can only pick up 4 heroes in the Dungeon, and. the only way to recruit new heroes is by dismissing the one currently in the group. The problem is that any gear removed from the dismissed cannot be placed on the newly recruited hero. It can’t even be sold to the merchant and basically clutters up the inventory window until the next dungeon is reached.
Selecting Characters – Multi-tasking can be in a pain the butt when you’re playing alone. Not because it’s difficult to move the heroes, but because you can’t always easily select them. The character portrait highlights are not easy to see, so at times a hero will be highlighted that you didn’t wish to move. Maybe a patch can allow us to scroll over the heroes to select them in Real-Time Strategy games.
That looks familiar – Even though there are tons of variations on rooms, the areas begin to look extremely similar really quickly. This tends to be a problem with Rogue-Likes in general with the need to focus on indoor grid design. It can bog down the exploration experience when one place looks a little too similar to the last.
Multiplayer Flaws – Dungeon of the Endless allows for players to reach 12 floors before completing the game. Players can stop and save anytime with one player, but Multiplayer does not have the option to save. This cuts down on the idea of exploration because games can take hours to complete. Also, items in chests are not distributed to multiple players. This would not be an issue if you could trade or door loot for a dungeon companion. Lastly, players can invite players to join a game but the option to create a private much does not exist.
Conclusion
The story is a little light but that’s typical of the genre. What you have instead is a fun time waster that quickly becomes addicting. Searching around for various characters, stacking resources, and exploring for loot is a blast! We recommend you go out and buy Dungeon of the Endless. Find four friends and explore the endless mystery that awaits you.

I still recommend this game because I have an amazing time in it, but, yeah.
